xslg.name: Expected Slugging (xSLG)
xslg.definition: How many total bases a hitter is expected to get per at-bat, based on how hard and at what angle the ball was hit. It strips out luck and defense.

brl_percent.name: Barrel Rate
brl_percent.definition: A barrel is a batted ball with an ideal combination of exit velocity and launch angle. Barrel Rate is how often a hitter makes that kind of high-quality contact.

hard_hit_percent.name: Hard-Hit Rate
hard_hit_percent.definition: Percentage of batted balls hit at 95 mph or higher. It shows how often a hitter makes hard contact with the ball.

xba.name: Expected Batting Average (xBA)
xba.definition: The batting average a player should have based on the quality of contact (exit velocity, launch angle, sprint speed), rather than the actual result of each ball in play.

xwoba.name: Expected wOBA
xwoba.definition: Expected weighted on-base average. A single number for overall offensive value that credits walks, singles and extra-base hits by how much they are worth, estimated from contact quality.

squared_up_rate.name: Squared-Up Rate
squared_up_rate.definition: How often a swing produces close to the maximum possible exit velocity for that bat speed and pitch speed. Higher means cleaner contact.

chase_percent.name: Chase Rate
chase_percent.definition: Percentage of pitches outside the strike zone that the hitter swings at. For hitters, lower is better. For pitchers it is flipped: a higher chase rate means they fool hitters more often.

k_percent.name: Strikeout Rate (K%)
k_percent.definition: Strikeouts divided by plate appearances. For hitters, lower is better. For pitchers, higher is better.

bb_percent.name: Walk Rate (BB%)
bb_percent.definition: Walks divided by plate appearances. For hitters, higher is better. For pitchers, lower is better.

whiff_percent.name: Whiff Rate
whiff_percent.definition: Percentage of swings that miss the ball entirely. For hitters, lower is better. For pitchers, higher is better.

bat_speed.name: Bat Speed
bat_speed.definition: Average speed of the sweet spot of the bat at contact. Faster swings produce harder-hit balls.

exit_velocity.name: Average Exit Velocity
exit_velocity.definition: The average speed of the ball right after it leaves the bat. For pitchers, a lower value means they are limiting hard contact.

xera.name: Expected ERA (xERA)
xera.definition: What a pitcher's ERA should be based on the quality of contact allowed, strikeouts and walks, rather than the runs that actually scored.

era.name: Earned Run Average (ERA)
era.definition: Earned runs allowed per nine innings pitched. The classic bottom-line pitching stat. Lower is better.

whip.name: WHIP
whip.definition: Walks And Hits per Inning Pitched. It shows how well a pitcher keeps runners off the bases: walks plus hits, divided by innings pitched. Lower is better; under 1.00 is excellent.

gb.name: Ground Ball Rate
gb.definition: Percentage of batted balls hit on the ground. Ground balls rarely become home runs, so a higher rate usually helps a pitcher.

fb_velocity.name: Fastball Velocity
fb_velocity.definition: Average speed of the pitcher's fastball.

extension.name: Extension
extension.definition: How far in front of the rubber the pitcher releases the ball. More extension makes a pitch look faster to the hitter.
